### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/flow.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via ApprovalNodeConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/flow.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `98054b2ce24fd0165ad7aa140f9147370a3971e4` — the merge of head `4823c579361ad3bfd8025170edac4fabe1ab6a4c` into base `42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 98054b2ce24fd0165ad7aa140f9147370a3971e4 && git checkout 98054b2ce24fd0165ad7aa140f9147370a3971e4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe 4823c579361ad3bfd8025170edac4fabe1ab6a4c && git checkout -B drift-repro 42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe && git merge --no-ff 4823c579361ad3bfd8025170edac4fabe1ab6a4c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 42d9fe8f5be01cf8822c324af6142103193199fe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25609 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T11:42Z · head `4823c57936` · report `6383750916` · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Both clause-② limbs hit (path: `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`; declaration: `Clause-②: yes`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is still owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25609`, no other closing keyword. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Ruling-ref: 6377731715` are line-initial in the body; the changeset carries both declarations, with `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`. Six files, +259/−1 (`get_files`), all inside the claim's surface: `approval.zod.ts`, a new test file, the generated `approval.mdx` row and `authorable-surface/automation.json` row, the `liveness/flow.json` `_note`, and the changeset. No runtime file (#25573 keeps that half), no governed path. `origin/main` was merged once (`481ac62116`) through `os-regen-merge.sh`.
2. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema.excludeSubmitter: z.boolean().optional()` sits on the node config (each approval step is a node, ADR-0019). It is absent when off, so every stored node and each request's config snapshot parse unchanged ("off, behaviour is unchanged" holds at the parse). The approver row and the flow node still refuse it as an unknown key. The describe opens with `[PLANNED — not yet enforced]`, defines the submitter (`submitter_id`, the run's trigger user), sends an emptied slate to `onEmptyApprovers` ("never passes silently"), and tells the author the engine does not read it yet.
3. **Gates.** Check-runs on `4823c57936` at this record: 23 success, 6 skipped, 11 in progress, 0 failed. Local, per the report: `--ran` 114/114 with no NOT MEASURED; spec 715 files / 21703 tests, typecheck clean; the new test file 16/16. Ablations: the key renamed, 10/16 red; `.optional()` → `.default(false)`, 2/16 red; both restored. Landing waits for every check green and the contract-review PASS.
4. **Deviations accepted.** (a) The PM's assumption of a `planned` ledger row was disproved by measurement: a row planted under `flow/nodes.config` makes `check:liveness` exit 1 ("declared children but property is not a container"), because the walk ends at a `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`. The record moved to a `_note` PLANNED RECORD sentence, following the `page.json` precedent, plus the describe marker and the authorable-surface row. Accepted. (b) A model-named trailer was amended to the model-free pair before any push. (c) `gen:docs` was run directly instead of `check:generated --fix` (then green). `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2.
5. **Open questions and out-of-scope outcomes.**
   - **`excludeSubmitter: true` beside `onEmptyApprovers: 'auto_approve'`:** an exclusion-emptied slate would be waved through, against the ruling's "never a silent pass". This is a contract-shape fork: A, the spec refuses the pair; B, the runtime overrides `auto_approve`; C, accept it. It goes to the maintainer in its own decision card (number below). It does not hold this PR: the key is unreleased, so adding a refusal before the next release narrows no published surface. The describe states the ruled invariant, which A or B makes true; under C the describe would change.
   - **Does the exclusion also screen the `fallbackApprovers` slate and `admin_rescue`?** A runtime choice inside the ruling ("the resolved approver set"), carried by #25573, the runtime half. That card's seat answers it, and the describe widens when it lands.
   - The liveness walk reaches no approval node-config key at all (`onEmptyApprovers`, `fallbackApprovers` included): Acceptance notes (a coverage observation, recorded in the PR body's Measured section).
   - The header of `ui/component-record-blocks-empty-state-24266.test.ts` claims a gate reads its `[PLANNED]` marker that none does: dropped — a comment inaccuracy with no reader.
6. **Landing.** Not governed, 260 changed lines. Once the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. On merge, #25573 (the runtime half) unblocks for its lane.

On the scope: `hits` is the one schema file. The cited files are every file its hunks make a claim about, read in the code: the liveness ledger and the gate that reads it (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` is `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts`; no `scripts/check-liveness*` exists), the FlowSchema door that judges an approval node's `config`, the executor and service the describe's "who the submitter is" and "the engine does not read this key" sentences are about, and the three ADRs the TSDoc and the ruling lean on. The rest of the diff (the changeset, the regenerated `authorable-surface/automation.json` and `references/automation/approval.mdx` rows, the test file) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, read here only where the schema hunk makes a claim about it.

Inputs: card #25609 (body; comments 6382817354, 6383187041, 6383750916), rulings 6377731715, 6377842908 and the reconciliation 6377965040 on #25496, runtime card #25573 (body; comments 6382188555, 6382833455), the PR body, its file list and the net diff against `main` at its head (merge-base `481ac6211641ccb7292508ed423f02e432322e4a` = `origin/main` at read time; 6 files, +259/−1), and the check-runs on the head. The PR's own comment thread was not read before this verdict was formed.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` gains `excludeSubmitter: z.boolean().optional()` — one new optional key on the approval node's `config`. Three doors widen together through the one schema: the direct parse; the `FlowSchema` per-node door (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts:174` registers `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` for `approval` nodes, which is why the key is refused today as `custom` at `nodes.N.config.excludeSubmitter`); and the executor's own `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema.safeParse(node.config ?? {})` (`approval-node.ts:161`). RIGHT — a widening; nothing that parsed before is refused.
2. No default: `.optional()`, not `.default(false)`. A node that omits the key parses byte-identical to before, so the `node_config_json` snapshot each request row keeps is unchanged, and `authorable-defaults/` correctly carries no new row. RIGHT — pinned by §1 "omitted stays absent" and §4 "no default".
3. The approver row (`ApprovalNodeApproverSchema`, a strictObject), the flow node beside `config`, and the flow root stay closed to the key — pinned by §3. RIGHT: one switch per node is the ruled "step-level option"; ADR-0019 D3 maps `steps[]` to successive approval nodes, so node config is the step.
4. Public surface: no export added or removed (`api-surface/` untouched is correct — it records export existence, not shape); `ApprovalNodeConfig` and `ApprovalNodeConfigParsed` gain one optional member; `getApprovalNodeConfigJsonSchema()` gains one optional boolean property under `additionalProperties: false` (pinned by §4). No exhaustive consumer of the key set exists on `origin/main` (only tests read individual `.shape` members), and objectui's `FlowNodeInspector` derives the approval node form from the engine-published configSchema, so no sibling hand-list goes stale. RIGHT.
5. Generated artifacts: the `authorable-surface/automation.json` row `automation/ApprovalNodeConfig:excludeSubmitter` and the `approval.mdx` row carry exactly the describe; the TSDoc's tracker ids do not project. RIGHT — `Type Check · source gates`, which runs `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs` and `check:generated --reconcile-only`, is green on this head.

The describe's statements, against the cited code:

- "the user whose action started the flow run, recorded on the approval request as `submitter_id`" — TRUE today. `approval-node.ts:196` passes `submitterId: runTriggerUser(context)`; `runTriggerUser` (`:107`) returns the recorded `triggerUserId` and otherwise `userId`; `approval-service.ts:3862` writes it as `submitter_id`; the column is `sys-approval-request.object.ts:307`.
- "The approval engine does not read this key yet, so today the submitter is NOT removed" — TRUE. `excludeSubmitter` has 0 hits on `origin/main`; the executor parses the whole config (`:161`) and reads none of it. Correctly marked: the describe opens with `[PLANNED — not yet enforced]` and closes with this sentence.
- "takes the node's `onEmptyApprovers` route (`admin_rescue` by default, or `fallbackApprovers` under `'fallback'`)" — PLANNED, and each named item is true of the enum (`onEmptyApprovers` defaults to `admin_rescue`; `fallbackApprovers` is paired by `checkFallbackApproversPairing`) and of the runtime routes (`approval-service.ts:3664` to `:3812`). The parenthetical is not exhaustive — the enum also has `fail` and `auto_approve`. A precision point for the #25573 rewrite, not a falsehood.
- "never passes silently" — the ruling's letter (6377731715 item 5; 6377842908 「排除后无人可批按 ADR-0042 升级」), marked planned. It is NOT derivable from the cited code for one legal pairing: under `onEmptyApprovers: 'auto_approve'` an empty slate opens no request and completes down the approve edge (`approval-service.ts:3674`, `approval-node.ts:221`). As written the describe therefore binds #25573 to make the invariant true (shape A or B in ③); it does not describe today's runtime and does not claim to.
- "the approval record shows that the exclusion changed the route" — planned, the runtime half, consistent with both rulings.
- The TSDoc's "ADR-0019 made each approval STEP an approval NODE" — TRUE (D1; the D3 re-home table).

The marker and the ledger:

- `[PLANNED — not yet enforced]` is the liveness vocabulary's `planned` marker (`check-liveness.mts:499`, `MARKER_RE.planned`). ADR-0049 applies in substance — a segregation-of-duties key is a control boundary, and the ADR allows exactly enforced, marked-as-not-enforced, or absent — and this key is marked, with the describe saying the submitter is not removed today. ADR-0049's letter spells the marker `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]`; the lane's precedents for a key with a named carrier (`ui/app.zod.ts:422`, `ui/component.zod.ts:1175`) use the PLANNED form, which is the more precise disposition here (a committed carrier, #25573). RIGHT.
- No ledger row is possible, as the `_note` claims: `flow.json` `nodes.children.config` is a leaf row (`live`, evidence in `service-automation/src/engine.ts`); `FlowNodeSchema.config` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`; `childShape()` (`check-liveness.mts:662`) returns `shapeOf(unknown)`, which is null; `drillChildren` (`:1067` to `:1070`) then reports `declared children but property is not a container` — the dev's measurement is what the code does. `_note` is free prose the gate never parses (no reference to it in check-liveness.mts). The `PLANNED RECORD` sentence follows `liveness/page.json`'s `_note` precedent for keys the walk cannot reach. `Spec property liveness` is green on this head. RIGHT.
- The window: once a runtime carries this spec, the designer offers the toggle with the PLANNED help text, and the key is carried unread until #25573 lands. That is the order the ruling chose ("spec first, then plugin-approvals"); the describe's last sentence is the only author-facing guard, the hand-written Approvals guide is deliberately not updated, and the PR records the window for release timing. Accepted as ruled; it sets the clock on open question 1 below.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor — RIGHT. `Metadata-protocol: added` (a new authorable key) takes at least minor on the package the diff moves. The PR's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is right: one optional key is added and nothing that parsed before is refused. Both declaration lines are present in the PR body and in `.changeset/25609-approval-exclude-submitter.md`; `Check Changeset` is green. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed (not breaking). No other published package moves — `plugin-approvals` is untouched and its behaviour on this head is unchanged. The changeset body carries no tracker id and no model identifier, and it tells the upgrading reader the key is declared ahead of the engine that honours it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6383750916, each flag answered:

open_questions

1. `excludeSubmitter: true` beside `onEmptyApprovers: 'auto_approve'` — ESCALATED TO THE MAINTAINER as a scoped follow-up to ruling 6377731715 item 5. The tension is in the ruling's own letter ("takes the node's existing onEmptyApprovers fallback … never a silent pass", while `auto_approve` IS the silent pass). My reading: shape A (a parse-time refinement in the `checkFallbackApproversPairing` style, refusing the pairing) makes the ruled invariant structurally true at the contract and keeps the runtime free of a policy override; shape B is acceptable; shape C contradicts the describe as written. Timing: A is a widening-era edit only until the first release carries this key — after that it is a `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with an ADR-0087 disposition. The maintainer should rule before the Version Packages PR that carries this spec minor, or knowingly accept that later cost. Not a FAIL point: the describe states only the ruled invariant, is marked planned, and the choice is not the dev's to make.
2. Whether the exclusion also screens the `fallbackApprovers` slate and the `admin_rescue` administrators — ESCALATED TO #25573, a runtime decision. The describe today says "the slate `approvers` resolves to", the ruling's literal "resolved approver set"; recommendation B (every slate the node opens on) for segregation of duties, with the describe widened when the runtime lands. Not blocking.

out_of_scope_findings

1. The liveness walk cannot reach any approval node config key — ACCEPTED as noted, not filed. A gate coverage gap, not a defect in this diff; `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` already holds the node-type to config-schema registry the walk could consult, so a spec-lane card is cheap if ledger coverage of node config keys is wanted. "carrier: none" stands.
2. A test header comment in `ui/component-record-blocks-empty-state-24266.test.ts` misattributes a marker read to the gate — ACCEPTED as noted; a comment-only inaccuracy outside this diff.

deviations

1. Ledger row measured impossible; shipped `_note` plus marker — ACCEPTED: measured, precedent-backed, and the gate is green.
2. First commit's model-named trailer amended before push — VERIFIED: all five non-merge commits on `origin/main..4823c57936` carry `Claude-Session:` plus the model-free co-author line; no pushed commit carries a model identifier.
3. PR body footer in the session-URL form — CORRECT per AGENTS.md.
4. `gen:docs` run directly rather than `check:generated --fix` — ACCEPTED: CI's `Type Check · source gates` ran `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` green on this head.
5. `test:repo` not run locally — ACCEPTED: `Test Core` is the record and is named below.
6. No reverse-verification for a cross-package type change — VERIFIED: no exhaustive consumer of the key set on `origin/main`; the only widening is an optional member.

Check-runs on the head (46 runs), read at 2026-10-24T12:05Z: every concluded run is `success` or `skipped` (opt-in harnesses and matrix placeholders); none is red. Four of the five required contexts are green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (all four lanes — `source gates`, `workspace`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; also green: `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`. NOT concluded at posting: `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)` are `in_progress`, so the bare required context `Test Core` has not reported; the other four shards concluded `success`. This verdict is on the contract; the queue still requires `Test Core` to conclude green before anything is armed.
